openUiAnatomy: no published Open UI checkbox anatomy consulted directly — union built from the three clones: Salt's Checkbox (a single <label> wrapping a real, visually-hidden native <input type="checkbox"> plus a CheckboxIcon box plus the label text as a sibling child — the label IS the whole clickable region), shadcn's Checkbox (a bare Radix CheckboxPrimitive.Root with no owned label — id/htmlFor association is entirely the consumer's job via a separate Label/FieldLabel component on a different canonical row), and M3's <md-checkbox> (a Lit custom element whose shadow DOM renders a real native <input type="checkbox"> UNDER three separately-opacity-animated layers — .outline, .background, .icon — plus a shared md-focus-ring and md-ripple, and no label of its own either).

behavior.pattern: A tri-state (checked / unchecked / indeterminate) toggle for an independent choice, per the W3C APG checkbox pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/checkbox/), which Salt's own usage.mdx cites directly. All three systems build it on a REAL native <input type="checkbox">, visually hidden and layered under a styled box — Salt and M3 confirmed by reading their component source [S]; shadcn/Radix is [R], reasoned from shadcn's own aria-checked selector usage (checkbox-demo.tsx's `has-[[aria-checked=true]]`) and the linked Radix docs, since primitives/ was not cloned (behavior-reference only, never a style source). The cross-system axes are: (1) who owns the label — Salt owns it as a `label` prop rendered INSIDE its own <label> element (so the whole label, icon included, is one native clickable region); shadcn and M3 own no label at all, and compose with the separate `label`/`field` canonical rows; (2) how the tri-state prop is shaped — Salt and M3 expose two independent booleans (`checked`, `indeterminate`, and a checkbox CAN receive both at once even though only one renders); shadcn/Radix collapses them into one `checked: boolean | "indeterminate"` prop, which is a real, sourced API-shape difference, not a cosmetic one; (3) whether a multi-checkbox GROUP construct exists at all — Salt ships `CheckboxGroup` (a <fieldset> with NO roving tabindex, confirmed absence of any keydown handler); shadcn and M3 have no dedicated group primitive (shadcn's own docs say to compose multiple `Field`s instead); (4) the validation/error tone — all three actually have one (a genuine cross-system rarity in this pipeline), but Salt alone has TWO tones (error, warning).
behavior.chassis: skeleton/checkbox.tsx — written from the template's part union: a root (a real

rows.note: Salt = "label-wrap": Checkbox.tsx returns ONE <label> whose children are the native <input>, the CheckboxIcon box, and the `label` prop's ReactNode, in that order [S]. Because it is a real <label>, clicking ANYWHERE inside it — including the label text — toggles the input via native browser semantics; this is not JS, it is what a <label> does. shadcn = "unwrapped" [R]: the rendered root owns no label at all; checkbox-demo.tsx pairs it with a SEPARATE <Label htmlFor> element on a different canonical row. M3 = "unwrapped" [S]: checkbox.ts's render() has no label anywhere in the shadow DOM; the component explicitly anticipates being placed INSIDE a consumer-authored <label> instead (see behavior.label-click-target). Rendering a <label> wrapper for all three would silently give shadcn and M3 label semantics neither actually has; rendering a bare wrapper for all three would destroy Salt's native click-target.

Salt [S] and M3 [S] both build on a REAL native <input type="checkbox">, visually hidden (opacity 0, absolutely positioned over the visual box) rather than simulated — Checkbox.tsx's <input ... type="checkbox" .../> and checkbox.ts's <input type="checkbox" .../> inside the shadow root are byte-legible. M3 additionally expands the input's hit area to a 48x48 INVISIBLE touch target when `touch-target="wrapper"` (`:host([touch-target='wrapper']) { margin: max(0px, ((48px - container-size) / 2)) }`, and the input itself is always 48x48 unless `touch-target="none"`) [S] — not modelled as its own row for scope reasons (a config axis with no cross-system counterpart to compare against; Salt's input is sized to the box itself with no separate touch-target concept). shadcn/Radix is [R]: its public API documents a hidden native `<input>` "bubble" for HTML form participation behind a styled non-input root, but primitives/ was not cloned to confirm the exact element, so this cell is an inference from Radix's published docs (linked directly from checkbox.mdx) rather than a grep.

M3 ONLY, and it is the one real structural fact this chassis does NOT fully reproduce (declared, not silent — see 'Declared approximations'). checkbox.ts's render() puts THREE separate absolutely-positioned <div>s inside `.container`: `.outline` (the 2px/0px border ring), `.background` (the primary-colour fill), and `.icon` (the mark) — each with its OWN opacity/transform transition, so the fill fades and scales in independently of the outline recolouring instantly [S, internal/_checkbox.scss lines ~99-148]. Salt's box is ONE element carrying border + background + icon-child together (CheckboxIcon.css has no equivalent layering) [S]. shadcn's box is likewise one element (the cva string puts border/bg classes directly on the root) [S]. The chassis renders one box element for all three; M3's independent fade-in is the thing lost.

THREE DIFFERENT STRATEGIES for the same two glyphs (a checkmark, a dash), and this is character, not decoration (CLAUDE.md law 3). Salt = "svg-plus-pseudo-dash": CheckboxIcon.tsx renders a REAL SolidCheckmark <svg> only when `checked && !indeterminate`, and a SEPARATE, lighter CheckmarkIcon svg when `checked && !indeterminate && readOnly` — TWO different checkmark assets depending on read-only — while the indeterminate dash is not an SVG at all, it is a plain CSS `::before` bar (`.saltCheckboxIcon-indeterminate::before { content:''; width: calc(size - 6px); height: 2px; background: currentColor }`) [S]. shadcn = "single-icon": Radix's `Indicator` renders its ONE child (a lucide CheckIcon) whenever `checked` is truthy — which includes the STRING "indeterminate" — so shadcn shows the IDENTICAL checkmark glyph for both checked and indeterminate; there is no dash anywhere in this component [S] — see state.indeterminate and finding 3. M3 = "dual-rect": checkbox.ts always renders `<svg class="icon"><rect class="mark short"/><rect class="mark long"/></svg>` UNCONDITIONALLY in the DOM, and CSS classes (`.checked` vs `.indeterminate`, both driven by the SAME two <rect> elements) rotate/scale them into either a checkmark or a flat dash via `transform` — one asset, two shapes, entirely CSS-driven [S, internal/_checkbox.scss lines 238-276].

Salt ONLY: `CheckboxGroup` (packages/core/src/checkbox/CheckboxGroup.tsx) renders a <fieldset> providing `disabled`/`readOnly`/`validationStatus`/`name`/`checkedValues` context to every child Checkbox — and NO roving tabindex: `useCheckboxGroup.ts` and `CheckboxGroupContext.ts` bind no keydown handler of any kind, so every checkbox in a Salt group keeps its own tab stop and only Tab/Shift+Tab move between them (accessibility.mdx confirms) [S]. `direction` ("horizontal"|"vertical", default vertical) is a real prop but not modelled as its own row for scope (a single Salt-only layout axis with no cross-system counterpart) [S]. shadcn: OFF, confirmed absence — no group component exists anywhere in this clone; the checkbox docs literally say "Use multiple fields to create a checkbox list" [S]. M3: OFF, confirmed absence — no group/set token family exists in _md-comp-checkbox.scss in either edition, and no companion navigation-style file references one [S]. There is no separate "checkbox-group" row in 04-component-map.md to send this to (unlike chip's pill-input, which had one) — it is Salt's own package's answer to the SAME canonical row's "many checkboxes" concern, so it is modelled here rather than dropped.

APG's checkbox pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/checkbox/, cited directly by Salt's own usage.mdx References section) specifies `role="checkbox"` with `aria-checked` true/false/mixed. Salt [S] and M3 [S] get this role IMPLICITLY and for free — it is a real native `<input type="checkbox">`, so the browser supplies the role and `checked`/`indeterminate` map to the accessibility tree without any explicit `role` or `aria-checked` attribute in source (M3's render() only writes an explicit `aria-checked="mixed"` for the indeterminate case, because native `<input>` semantics do not otherwise expose "mixed" — confirmed by checkbox_test.ts asserting exactly `aria-checked` toggles to/from `'mixed'`, and nothing else). shadcn/Radix is [R]: the linked Radix docs and shadcn's own `has-[[aria-checked=true]]` selector in checkbox-demo.tsx together indicate the rendered root exposes `role="checkbox"`/`aria-checked` the same way, but the exact element and its ARIA wiring are not independently confirmable without primitives/ cloned.

SPACE ONLY, in all three — and it is worth stating plainly because it is the OPPOSITE of chip's action pills (Enter+Space) and the exact match of native `<input type="checkbox">` semantics, which none of the three systems override. Salt's accessibility.mdx: "Space changes the state of the checkbox, select or deselect" [S], and there is no keydown override anywhere in Checkbox.tsx — the browser does the whole job. M3: same, no keydown handler in checkbox.ts — the native input does it [S]. shadcn/Radix: [R], per the linked Radix docs and the general APG pattern; not independently confirmable without primitives/. Enter does nothing in any column — a real, sourced absence (native `<input type="checkbox">` does not respond to Enter, only Space).

Salt: the ENTIRE label — box AND text — is one native click target, because structure.shell="label-wrap" makes it a real <label> [S]. shadcn: only the small box itself toggles; extending the click target to label text requires the CONSUMER'S OWN separate <Label htmlFor> to do it via native label semantics, which is outside this component (declared composition, see slot.composes) [S/R]. M3 does NOT merely lack this — it explicitly ANTICIPATES being wrapped in a consumer-authored <label> and redirects that click to its own internal input: checkbox.ts's constructor adds a click listener that calls `isActivationClick`/`dispatchActivationClick` from `internal/events/form-label-activation.js`, so "click bubbled from an ancestor <label>" is a real, sourced code path even though M3 renders no label of its own [S].

checked / unchecked / indeterminate, and clicking or spacing an INDETERMINATE checkbox resolves to CHECKED in every column — this is native `<input type="checkbox">` behaviour (a user interaction always toggles `.checked` and clears `.indeterminate`, regardless of which was previously true), which Salt and M3 inherit for free by using a real input: Salt's `handleChange` reads `event.target.checked` post-toggle [S] and a `useIsomorphicLayoutEffect` keeps `input.indeterminate` in sync with the `indeterminate` PROP reactively (`inputRef.current.indeterminate = indeterminate ?? false`) rather than driving it through render, because `indeterminate` has no HTML ATTRIBUTE form, only an IDL/DOM-property form [S]. M3's `handleInput` reads BOTH `target.checked` and `target.indeterminate` back off the native element after the browser has already resolved them [S]. shadcn/Radix: [R] — its own `checked` prop accepts `boolean | "indeterminate"`, and shadcn's OWN data-table example (`components/cards/payments.tsx`) proves the round-trip: `onCheckedChange={(value) => table.toggleAllPageRowsSelected(!!value)}` receives a plain boolean on click even from an indeterminate header checkbox [S, a real citation, not a doc-only inference].

Salt: NO roving tabindex — CONFIRMED ABSENCE. `internal/useCheckboxGroup.ts` and `internal/CheckboxGroupContext.ts` bind no keydown handler of any kind; every checkbox in a group keeps its own tab stop, Tab/Shift+Tab only (accessibility.mdx) [S] — the same answer PillGroup gave in CHIP-MATRIX.md finding 7, and the opposite of InteractableCardGroup's roving-tabindex radiogroup. shadcn/M3: OFF, no group construct to navigate (see structure.group).

THE MECHANISM, not the colour (see prop.validation / style.box.validation for those). Salt computes `validationStatus` in JS and DELIBERATELY SUPPRESSES it when disabled: `const validationStatus = !disabled ? (checkboxGroup?.validationStatus ?? formFieldValidationStatus ?? validationStatusProp) : undefined` [S] — a disabled+error Salt checkbox never shows the error tone, by source logic, not by CSS specificity. shadcn exposes `aria-invalid` as a bare boolean the consumer sets [S, checkbox-invalid.tsx passes a literal `aria-invalid` prop with no value]; there is no equivalent JS-level disabled-suppression visible in this file, so the chassis does not invent one for that column. M3 has a full parallel `error-*` token family (state-layer AND outline colours) covering every interaction state, but — being tokens-only for the STYLE half and [R] for the trigger mechanism — there is no element to confirm HOW `error` gets turned on (likely a boolean attribute per the general M3 spec, but not grep-able here).

Salt: the native `disabled` attribute on the input (ORed with the group's `disabled`), plus a `.saltCheckbox-disabled` class driving a blanket opacity on the WHOLE label [S]. shadcn: native `disabled`, `disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-50` [S]. M3: native `?disabled` on the input, PLUS a genuinely interesting sourced detail — `:where(.disabled, .prev-disabled) :is(.background, .icon, .mark) { animation-duration: 0s; transition-duration: 0s }` with the source comment "Don't animate to/from disabled states... Without this, there'd be a FOUC if the checkbox state is programmatically changed while disabled" [S] — M3 explicitly SUPPRESSES its own transition system around the disabled boundary, a mechanism neither other system has because neither other system animates state changes at all (see style.box.transition).

Salt ONLY — and the sourced nuance is that the native HTML `readonly` IDL attribute has NO EFFECT on `type="checkbox"` inputs per the WHATWG HTML spec [R, spec fact, not Salt-specific], so Salt's `readOnly` prop is NOT relying on the browser at all: `handleChange` does its own early return, `if (event.nativeEvent.defaultPrevented || readOnly) { return; }` [S] — Salt implements read-only in application JS, dresses the input with `readOnly`/`aria-readonly` anyway (harmless, browser ignores it), and separately dashes the box border and swaps to a lighter checkmark glyph (`CheckmarkIcon` instead of `CheckmarkSolidIcon`) [S, CheckboxIcon.tsx, CheckboxIcon.css `.saltCheckboxIcon-readOnly`]. shadcn: OFF, confirmed absence — no readOnly/readonly concept anywhere in checkbox.tsx. M3: OFF, confirmed absence — no readonly-* token in either edition of _md-comp-checkbox.scss.

M3 is the most explicit of the three: a full form-associated custom element — `getFormValue` (returns `null` when unchecked OR indeterminate, `value` otherwise), `getFormState`, `formResetCallback`, `formStateRestoreCallback`, and a real `CheckboxValidator` that LAZILY CREATES A REAL native `<input type="checkbox">` purely to borrow its constraint-validation engine (`this.checkboxControl.checked = ...; this.checkboxControl.required = ...; return this.checkboxControl.validity`) [S] — M3 delegates its OWN validity computation to a second, invisible, native checkbox rather than reimplementing the algorithm. Salt: inherits native form participation for free because its own input IS the real form control [S]. shadcn/Radix: [R] — the linked Radix docs describe a hidden native input for the same purpose, not independently confirmable here.

A real API-SHAPE divergence, not a styling one. Salt [S] and M3 [S] both expose `checked?: boolean` and `indeterminate?: boolean` as TWO INDEPENDENT props — you CAN pass `checked={true} indeterminate={true}` simultaneously (both components then choose which one WINS visually: Salt's CheckboxIcon gates the checkmark on `checked && !indeterminate`; M3's render() computes `isChecked = checked && !indeterminate` the same way) — so "two-boolean" is the value for both. shadcn/Radix [S, sourced from shadcn's own `payments.tsx`, not merely the linked docs]: ONE `checked` prop typed `boolean | "indeterminate"` — the type system makes "checked AND indeterminate" literally inexpressible, a different and narrower contract than the other two systems offer. "two-boolean" is value[0] because it is the shape TWO of three systems actually use.

Salt ["off","error","warning"], SOURCE-DEFAULT-FIRST (`validationStatus?: AdornmentValidationStatus`, undefined/off by default) [S] — and Salt's own prop comment states plainly that "success" is accepted by the TYPE but renders no styling at all, which is why it is not listed as a third value here (a capability the type permits but the CSS never expresses is not a real value — see CHIP-MATRIX finding-2's class of defect). shadcn ["off","error"]: `aria-invalid` is a bare boolean — there is no "warning" concept anywhere in this component [S]. M3 ["off","error"]: a full `error-*` token family exists (state-layer AND outline colours, in both the selected and unselected sub-families) [S], but no `warning-*` family exists anywhere in either edition of _md-comp-checkbox.scss — CONFIRMED ABSENCE, grepped directly. Salt is therefore the only column with two validation tones; the other two agree with each other and disagree with Salt.

[false,true] — CAPABILITY LIST, all three [S]: Salt `disabled?: boolean` (ORed with the group's), shadcn native `disabled` (a real HTML attribute Radix forwards), M3 `@property({type:Boolean}) disabled` (inherited from LitElement's reflected-property convention, native `?disabled=${this.disabled}` on the shadow input).
Salt ONLY: [false,true] [S] — see behavior.readonly for the sourced nuance that this is Salt's own JS logic, not the native (spec-inert) HTML attribute. shadcn and M3: OFF, confirmed absence.

M3: [false,true] [S] — `@property({type:Boolean}) required`, wired directly into `CheckboxValidator`'s constraint-validation computation (`this.checkboxControl.required = state.required`). Salt: [false,true] but only reachable THROUGH `inputProps.required` — `CheckboxProps` itself has no top-level `required` field (it extends `Omit<InputHTMLAttributes<HTMLLabelElement>, ...>`, and `required` is not a valid attribute of a <label>), so a consumer must thread it via the escape-hatch `inputProps` object to land it on the real <input> [S] — a genuinely different, more indirect API shape than M3's first-class reflected property, worth carrying as a value rather than smoothing into an identical capability. shadcn: [false,true] [R] — Radix's published API includes `required`, not independently confirmable without primitives/ cloned.

Salt ONLY owns this slot — `label?: ReactNode`, rendered as the LAST child inside the component's own <label> element, so it participates in native label-click semantics for free (see structure.shell / behavior.label-click-target) [S]. shadcn and M3: OFF — neither renders any label text of its own; the visible label a consumer sees always belongs to a SEPARATE component on the `label`/`field` canonical rows, associated externally via `id`/`htmlFor` (shadcn: `<Checkbox id="terms"/><Label htmlFor="terms">...</Label>` — checkbox-demo.tsx, checkbox-basic.tsx) [S]. This is the same slot-ownership contrast BADGE-MATRIX.md drew for `structure.label-format`: one system formats/owns content the others treat as fully external.

DECLARED COMPOSITION, same convention as badge.template.json's slot.composes: (a) `label` — shadcn's and M3's external label association (both already-scoped canonical rows, `label` and `field` in 04-component-map.md's Forms & inputs section, neither built yet); (b) `field` — shadcn's own FieldDescription/FieldGroup/Field wrapper pattern for helper text and the `data-invalid`/`data-disabled` container styling seen in checkbox-invalid.tsx / checkbox-disabled.tsx, and Salt's `useFormFieldProps()` pulling `aria-describedby`/`aria-labelledby`/disabled/readOnly/validationStatus down from an ancestor form-field [S, both directions]; (c) `radio-group` — the sibling canonical row for the mutually-exclusive case, explicitly NOT this component (Salt's usage.mdx: "When the checkbox displays a mutually exclusive choice ... Instead, use RadioButton") [S]. All render as neutral placeholders in the harness rather than importing those skeletons.

Unchecked, enabled, unfocused. Salt: a neutral gray-500 outline (mode-invariant) on a white/near-black container fill — never filled solid, an outline-style box at every state [S]. shadcn: an --input-coloured 1px border with NO background at all in light mode, and a translucent input-tinted fill ONLY in dark mode (`dark:bg-input/30`, with no light-mode equivalent) — a real light/dark ASYMMETRY, not just a colour inversion [S]. M3: a 2px on-surface-variant outline with the fill layer present in the DOM but opacity:0 [S].

THREE DIFFERENT VISUAL STRATEGIES for the same boolean — the headline finding of this component. Salt: the fill NEVER changes (confirmed: no background rule anywhere keys off checked) — only the OUTLINE recolours to accent blue and a checkmark glyph appears in the same blue. It stays an outline box, permanently [S]. shadcn: a SOLID fill appears (`bg-primary`), the border recolours to match, and the icon becomes `text-primary-foreground` — a genuinely filled box [S]. M3: the fill (already in the DOM at opacity:0) fades AND scales in (`transform: scale(0.6)` → `scale(1)`, 350ms emphasized-decelerate) while the outline's width animates to 0 — fill REPLACES stroke, the identical mechanism CHIP-MATRIX.md documented for M3's `elevation@elevated` and `flat-selected` rows [S].

Salt: the box resets to its NEUTRAL (unselected) colours even if `checked` is also true — CheckboxIcon.css's compound `.saltCheckboxIcon-checked.saltCheckboxIcon-indeterminate` rule overrides BACK to the plain `selectable-borderColor`/`-foreground`, so an indeterminate Salt checkbox is grey with a grey dash, never blue [S]. shadcn: NO INDETERMINATE-SPECIFIC RULE EXISTS AT ALL — the cva string only keys off `data-[state=checked]`, never `data-[state=indeterminate]` — so an indeterminate shadcn checkbox renders with the RESTING (unstyled, un-filled) box colours while the Indicator STILL shows the checkmark glyph (Radix's Indicator renders on any truthy `checked`, including the string "indeterminate") [S] — a checkmark floating on an unstyled box, a real and slightly surprising defect-shaped finding, see 'Findings' below. M3: SAME visual treatment as checked — `.selected` (which the render() function sets for `isChecked || isIndeterminate`) covers both, and the dash-shaped mark is drawn in the identical primary/on-primary colour pair as the checkmark [S].

Salt: recolours the outline AND icon to the accent-tinted hover variant (`selectable-borderColor-hover`/`-foreground-hover`), keyed off the ROOT's `:hover` — so hovering the label TEXT hovers the box too, consistent with structure.shell [S]. shadcn: OFF — CONFIRMED ABSENCE, no `hover:` class of any kind anywhere in checkbox.tsx, unlike almost every other shadcn component this pipeline has built. M3: an 8%-opacity on-surface-tinted state layer (unselected) or primary-tinted (selected) [S].

Salt: `outline: 2px dotted accent-stronger` at a 1px offset PLUS the whole hover recolour riding along, keyed off the INPUT's `:focus-visible` via an adjacent-sibling selector [S]. shadcn: the familiar translucent 3px `ring-ring/50` box-shadow plus a border recolour [S]. M3: a 2px on-surface (unselected) outline recolour plus a 12%-opacity state layer — AND a SEPARATE `md-focus-ring` element exists in the real DOM that this chassis does not reproduce (declared, see 'Declared approximations') [S].

M3 ONLY models a true pressed/active state — a 12%-opacity state layer, tinted PRIMARY when the box is CURRENTLY unselected (i.e. the ripple previews the colour you are ABOUT to select into) and tinted ON-SURFACE when the box is currently selected (previewing the colour you are about to lose) — a real, sourced, symmetrical piece of design intent [S, selected-pressed-state-layer-color: on-surface vs unselected-pressed-state-layer-color: primary]. Salt: OFF — CONFIRMED ABSENCE, no `:active` selector anywhere in Checkbox.css or CheckboxIcon.css. shadcn: OFF — same, no `active:` class exists.

THREE DIFFERENT OPACITIES for the same idea — Salt 0.4 (a literal, blanket, on the whole label) [S], shadcn 0.5 (`disabled:opacity-50`) [S], M3 0.38 (`disabled-container-opacity` / `selected-disabled-container-opacity`, both 0.38 in this edition, applied only to the outline/background layers, never the icon) [S]. Three systems, three magnitudes: 0.38 / 0.4 / 0.5, none of them shared.

Salt: `size-selectable`, 12/14/16/18px by DENSITY — the same token chip's check-box part and badge's dot-detection logic both cite [S]. shadcn: `size-4` = 16px, fixed, no density capability [S]. M3: `container-size` = 18px, a hardcoded literal in both editions [S]. Applied to the input too so the (invisible) hit area always matches the visible box exactly.

Salt: `corner-weaker` → `curve-50` → 1/2/3/4px by DENSITY, collapsing to 0px under the sharp corner edition (the exact CHIP-MATRIX finding-1 token) [S]. shadcn: `rounded-[4px]`, a literal, density-invariant [S]. M3: `container-shape` = 2px, a hardcoded literal in all four logical corners, both editions [S].

Salt: `size-fixed-100` = 1px, on the FIXED (density-invariant) scale by design [S]. shadcn: a bare `border` utility = 1px, undeclared width, the same unvendored-Tailwind caveat every prior shadcn column has recorded [S]. M3: `unselected-outline-width` = 2px (this is the REST/unselected value; style.box.checked overrides it to 0 — see that row) [S].

Salt: Icon defaults to `--saltIcon-size: 100%`, filling whatever box it is placed in — Salt sizes its glyph RELATIVE to the box rather than with its own fixed number [S]. shadcn: `size-3.5` = 14px, fixed inside a 16px box [S]. M3: `icon-size` = 18px, EQUAL to `container-size` — the glyph fills the box exactly, no margin [S].

Salt ONLY: `gap: spacing-100` = 4/8/12/16px by density, between the box and the label text [S]. shadcn and M3: OFF — neither owns a label, so neither has anything of its own to space (a consumer's own flex row supplies whatever gap it likes, harness chrome, not a component token).

Salt: `cursor-hover` = pointer, on the whole label [S]. shadcn: OFF — CONFIRMED ABSENCE, no `cursor-pointer` class anywhere at rest (only `disabled:cursor-not-allowed` exists — see style.box.disabled); the resting cursor is whatever the underlying element's UA default is, which is not independently confirmable without primitives/ cloned. M3: `:host { cursor: pointer }`, explicit [S].

Salt ONLY: the body text role — REGULAR weight (400) at 11/14 . 12/16 . 14/18 . 16/20px by density, Open Sans [S] — the label text's own typography, since Salt owns that slot. shadcn and M3: OFF — the label text belongs to an external, not-yet-built component (see slot.composes).

The unchecked/enabled/unfocused box. Salt: neutral gray-500 border (MODE-INVARIANT — next/palette/neutral.css declares `--salt-palette-neutral` identically in the light and dark blocks, the same mode-invariance BADGE-MATRIX.md documented for `palette-accent`), on a white/near-black container fill [S]. shadcn: an --input-coloured border with NO background in light mode and a translucent fill ONLY in dark mode — see state.rest [S]. M3: a 2px on-surface-variant outline, transparent/invisible fill (opacity 0 — see structure.outline-layer for the layer this collapses) [S].

See state.checked for the three-way narrative. Salt: border-color and icon `color` both move to accent blue-500 (MODE-INVARIANT); the fill is UNTOUCHED [S]. shadcn: `border-primary bg-primary text-primary-foreground` — a real filled box [S]. M3: `border-width: 0` (the outline is removed, not merely recoloured — the CHIP-MATRIX `elevation@elevated` mechanism again), `background-color: primary` at full opacity, icon `on-primary` [S].

Salt: RESETS to the plain neutral/unselected colours (see structure.mark and 'Findings' — a real, sourced compound-selector override, reproduced here for free because `:checked:not(:indeterminate)` and `:indeterminate` are mutually exclusive selectors, so no cascade-order trick is needed) [S]. shadcn: OFF — CONFIRMED ABSENCE, no `data-[state=indeterminate]` rule exists anywhere in checkbox.tsx, so the box stays at its RESTING colours while the icon (see structure.mark) still shows a checkmark — see finding 3 [S]. M3: identical treatment to checked — `.selected` covers `isChecked || isIndeterminate` as one class [S].

Salt ONLY — the ACTUAL glyph that communicates indeterminate, since style.box.indeterminate resets Salt's colours to neutral (making an indeterminate box otherwise indistinguishable from a rest one). CheckboxIcon.css `.saltCheckboxIcon-indeterminate::before { content:''; position:absolute; top:50%; left:50%; width: calc(var(--checkbox-size) - 6px); height:2px; background: currentColor; transform: translate(-50%,-50%) }` — a plain CSS bar, not an svg [S]. shadcn: OFF — no dash of any kind; its indeterminate reuses the checkmark icon (see structure.mark). M3: OFF — its indeterminate glyph is the `.mark` <rect> pair rotated flat by CSS transform (structure.mark), not a separate pseudo-element.

Salt: border-color and icon colour move to the `-hover` variants of whichever base they were already on (selected or not) [S]. shadcn: OFF — CONFIRMED ABSENCE, no hover rule of any kind (see state.hover).
